cost.text: This path accepts whatever audits refiners already hold, without checking that they cover ILO child-labour and forced-labour standards or the mixing of hand-dug cobalt (I3, K3). It also has no plan for fixing abuse or helping affected children, so it could find a problem and then do nothing about it (K1).

speed.text: Keeping deliveries going under the export quotas is reasonable, and the clause on fixing problems rather than dropping suppliers is the right idea (D3, K1). The condition is that refiner disclosure has a fixed deadline that does not wait for each renewal, because contracts that renew late would otherwise leave workers' risk unchecked the longest (M1).

responsible.text: This is the only path that sets deadlines for audits based on ILO standards, includes private worker interviews and a safe way to report problems, and pays for fixes instead of walking away (K1, K3, M4). It also covers routes that do not go through IXM, which answers my round 1 concern that treating IXM as the only path could hide other routes (I1, T1).

challenge.text: Even the responsible path makes site labour checks depend on supplier mapping that may never be finished or honest, because the trail already goes cold after the trader and nothing yet links any refiner to a product (M1, M2). If suppliers have not named their refiners with chain-of-custody records by the deadline, the company should treat that silence as unresolved risk and send labour checks along the documented TFM-to-IXM route anyway, not keep waiting.

revised_recommendation: I changed my view and now accept Procurement's point that the company should map its own refiners before paying for an audit at TFM, because nothing links TFM to its batteries (M2), but only if the mapping has a fixed deadline and missing it automatically triggers labour checks.
condition_for_approval: I approve only if refiner audits must be independent and based on ILO child-labour and forced-labour standards, every mine or route the mapping finds (or that suppliers fail to rule out by the deadline) gets private worker interviews and a reporting channel, and any abuse found is fixed with the supplier, including help for affected children, rather than ended by dropping the supplier.

cost.text: Asking suppliers for whatever water, tailings and emissions data they already hold could let company statements count as evidence, when the file has no measured environmental data at all (M4). The plan also has no deadline or plan for what happens if suppliers say nothing, so the gap at the refiner, the step most likely to pollute and the one we cannot see, could stay open forever (I2, M1).

speed.text: Asking for independent environmental data at each renewal is acceptable only if every contract gets a final cut-off date, so contracts that renew late do not leave the gap open the longest (M4, D3). Backup suppliers brought in because of the export quotas must hand over the same measured environmental data before they are used, not after (D3, M1).

responsible.text: This is the only strategy that openly says the environmental picture is blank and makes measured water, tailings and emissions data a contract condition (M4). It must also add an action to collect greenhouse gas figures per tonne for each step, which it lists as needed but never assigns to anyone (M4, I2).

challenge.text: Greenhouse gas figures per tonne for the mine, the shipping leg and refining appear only under verification_needed, and no strategy gives anyone the job of collecting them, so the emissions gap has no owner. The cost strategy's environmental step also accepts data suppliers already hold without requiring that it be independent and measured, which repeats the problem that silence or self-reporting gets taken for safety.

revised_recommendation: I accept Procurement's point that environmental data can be phased in at renewal rather than freezing current orders under the quotas (D3), but I still insist that the data be independent and measured, that the refiner be named so it can be checked, and that a fixed final deadline apply to every contract.
condition_for_approval: I approve only if the chosen strategy requires independent, measured water-quality, tailings-dam and emissions data, plus greenhouse gas figures per tonne, for the mine and the named refiner by a fixed date with a named owner, and makes no green or low-impact claims until that data exists (M4, I2, M1).

cost.text: The refiner questionnaire and the risk register are the right first steps and match what due-diligence expectations generally ask for (M1, M2, K1, K2). But supplier answers and existing refiner audits must be recorded as unverified claims until chain-of-custody records back them, or the company may believe its chain is mapped when it is not (I3).

speed.text: Phasing hard conditions in at renewal is acceptable under the export quotas (D3), but a non-binding request for refiner names leaves import-control exposure open for every contract that renews late (M1, I3). Any backup or substitute supply must meet the full checks before the first order, with no quota-driven exceptions (D3, I2).

responsible.text: This is the only strategy that could eventually show whether the company's cobalt is kept apart from hand-dug sources, which is the open question for forced-labour import controls (I3, K3, M1). Using renewals rather than current orders for the hard conditions keeps the supply-gap risk manageable (D3).

challenge.text: None of the three strategies gives anyone the job of getting an official registry extract for TFM, even though the ownership conflict appears under verification needed. The responsible strategy's public reporting step covers only the environmental gap, so disclosures could still present CMOC's ownership and the reported Gécamines stake as settled when they are not (M3, I4, D1).

revised_recommendation: I now accept Procurement's point that hard evidence conditions can be phased in at contract renewal instead of blocking current orders, but I still hold that refiner disclosure, the risk register and full checks on any substitute supply must start now and be binding.
condition_for_approval: Approve only if refiner naming with chain-of-custody records has a fixed deadline for every supplier whatever its renewal date, substitute supply passes the same checks before first order, and the risk register, including the unresolved ownership items, is reviewed before any public disclosure.
